column1: # The record's VALUATION trajectory, from Robert Shiller's ie_data.xls (econ.yale.edu/~shiller/data,
# file last saved 2023-09-17; monthly, CAPE defined 1881.01-2023.09). Measured 2026-08-30. This is
# the evidence base for the slow-valuation-cycle mechanism: what the model's log(price/fair) should
# look like if CAPE is accepted as the record's fair-value proxy.
# THE COMMENSURABILITY JUDGMENT, stated once: the model's fair value is its own state variable;
# the record has no observable fair value, and CAPE (real price over 10y-smoothed real earnings) is
# a PROXY whose level drifts across eras (mean 16.0 over 1881-2023, 25.8 over 1990-2023). Anything
# derived from this file therefore ships as a BAND with judgment-set width, or as a diagnostic —
# never as a point-fidelity ratio. Dispersion is measured on log CAPE about the full-period mean.
# sd_logcape rows: the dispersion the model's sd log(p/f) is compared against (model at 0.22.1
# defaults: 0.102, median century — a 4x gap even against the calmest modern window).
# episode rows: the six deepest real-price declines, endpoints at monthly resolution, classified by
# the MODEL'S OWN rule (fundamentalLed: fundamental fell at least half the price fall), with REAL
# EARNINGS standing in for the fundamental. peak_rel = CAPE at the pre-decline peak over the
# 1881-2023 mean (16.0). What it shows: deep declines START ELEVATED — median peak_rel ~1.5x,
# 2.0-2.7x for 1929 and 2000 — where every deep model crash starts at 1.0x fair; and the led-MIX
# (3 fundamental / 3 valuation here vs the model's 40/60 at >35%) is closer than the peak
# valuations are, so the mechanism gap is the MANIA, not the mix. Note 2000-03 classifies
# FUNDAMENTAL under this rule — reported real earnings halved in 2001-02 — although its peak is the
# most valuation-extreme on record; the classifier and the peak column answer different questions.
